classification.difficultyReason: Identify the ladder as the hypotenuse and calculate the horizontal distance in a practical right-triangle problem.

content.prompt: A ladder of length 410 cm is leaning against a wall. It touches the wall 400 cm above the ground. What is the distance between the foot of the ladder and the wall?

spec.description: Ladder rising from level ground to a vertical wall, with a right-angle marker at the wall base. The 410 cm label belongs to the ladder; a curved pointer associates 400 cm with the wall height. Decorative brick texture and fill are omitted. Ordinary source blue and dotted red strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The ladder is the 410 cm hypotenuse; the vertical leg is 400 cm; the horizontal leg is unknown. Drawing proportions do not establish dimensions.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the distance from the foot of the ladder to the wall, in centimetres. The ladder is the hypotenuse.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+400^2&=410^2\\x^2+160000&=168100\\x^2&=168100-160000\\x^2&=8100\\x&=\sqrt{8100}\\x&=90\end{align*}$$

The distance is $90\text{ cm}$.
